title: The revocation appended a suffix to the holder's assignment identifier for its end command, so a valid 128-character assignment identifier made the command identifier invalid and failed the whole revoke transaction
resolution: The end command identifier comes from the port RevocationCommandIds, a deterministic derivation that must be bounded; B derives it as a SHA-256 digest. A test with the longest assignment identifier fails before the fix with invalid.

title: The grace age does not stop the sweep from discarding the version of an add-slot command delayed past it between its store and its add commit, so the record could name a discarded version
resolution: Not fixed: closing the window needs a claim shared by the add transaction and the sweep, but contract section 6.2 keeps SlotCredentials outside CapacityTransaction, and Q4 and accepted deviation 1 chose the grace age; left for the coordinator.

title: The rotation interleavings that contract section 9 requires were untested: two rotations reading one revision, a later switch before an earlier cleanup, and a higher orphan removed by the next rotation
resolution: In-memory tests with one-shot hooks cover another rotation between store and switch, a switch before an earlier cleanup, and a higher orphan; PostgreSQL tests gate two switches after their held count read and assert the loser's retry and conflict; three mutants fail them.

title: No test removed a reserved active slot to show the credential destroyed, no cancellation command, the reservation kept until the terminal fact, and the re-delivery refused
resolution: A PostgreSQL test removes the slot of a launched attempt with an earlier delivery, checks each effect, refuses the re-delivery with removed, and releases the reservation at the drain; two mutants fail it.
